Checkpoint 42 — R2-final: durable panel DBs + storm-proof rollout/probes

Checkpoint 42 — R2-final: durable panel DBs + storm-proof rollout/probes

What landed (manifests + new PVC, all applied live)

Change Why
manifests/control-panel-pvc.yaml (new): 1Gi RWO, local-path Panel DBs must survive pod redeploys, not just container restarts
Deployment volumes.data: emptyDir → PVC same; SESSIONS_DB + NODES_DB both live under /var/lib/ldndrc on the PVC
SESSIONS_DB env now actually live (was missing in-cluster; repo had it, cluster didn't) R2 session records were still in-memory-only in production
strategy: maxSurge 0 / maxUnavailable 1 hostNetwork pod binds node :8082; a surge pod deadlocks forever (CP-20 §6). This formalizes delete-old-first — future rollout restart should behave, but delete-pod stays the habit until proven
Probes pinned host: 127.0.0.1 root cause of the restart storm (below)
K3S_JOIN_URL → https://192.168.1.42:6443 stale .37 value; IP churn makes this a moving target (DHCP reservation = standing debt)

Two root-cause discoveries (both from the same churn family)

  1. 141-restart crashloop storm (panel RestartedCount 95→101→141 over 3 days). hostNetwork pod's probes default to the podIP — baked in at pod creation. The laptop's DHCP lease drifted (.37 → .65 → .42), the baked IP went dead, liveness killed the container, and kubelet restarted it inside the same sandbox with the same stale IP → permanent crashloop. Fix: loopback probes. Post-fix: the identical server has run 3d6h+ with 0 restarts.
  2. Pod-network outage (blocked the PVC bind). The first apply left the new pod Pending: rancher.io/local-path was alive but its reflector had dial tcp 10.43.0.1:443: no route to host — no pod-network pod could reach the service ClusterIP (proved with a scratch pod + wget). Same stale-flannel/iptables family as #1. Fix needed sudo systemctl restart k3s (user-run, Oct 27) → PVC bound, cluster healthy.

Durability proof (the R2-final headline)

  1. Login as durability → POST /api/sessions → 202, SID 117fd258af33 (Deployment + Service + 5Gi PVC created, all bound).
  2. kubectl delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ldndrc-control-panel — the exact operation that used to wipe every session record.
  3. Fresh pod ready in ~5s; boot log: sessions reconcile: 1 adopted, 0 tombstoned — records loaded from the PVC and the live Deployment adopted.
  4. GET /api/sessions from a fresh login → 117fd258af33 still there, provisioning → pod shortly 1/1 Running (real workspace image, left running for use).

The memory-hole that motivated R2 is closed: panel redeploys no longer lose sessions.

Known cost of the emptyDir → PVC swap

The old pod's nodes.json went with the emptyDir. Approved-laptop registrations from the rehearsal are gone; laptops re-join via the join TUI (same flow as before). downloads.json had no legacy data.

Side discovery: parallel in-flight work

The worktree holds an uncommitted, complete second chunk from Oct 27–30: the LAN onboarding portal (its own CP-41). Tests green, docs written, not deployed. Committed as its own commit immediately after this one (manifest's DOWNLOADS_DB block was surgically separated so neither commit carries the other's work). Nothing in that chunk was modified beyond one manifest comment refresh to match the new PVC reality (its "emptyDir caveat" text was honest then; the store now lives on the PVC).

Deploy state after this chunk

  • Cluster = repo manifest (applied Oct 27, verified today): PVC-backed, loopback probes, safe strategy, SESSIONS_DB + stale join URL fixed.
  • Panel image ldndrc/control-panel:dev (imported Oct 26) predates the portal code — env DOWNLOADS_DB is live but dormant until a rebuild. Portal deploy = next chunk's rebuild + import + delete-pod rollout.
  • Durability session 117fd258af33 left Running for use.

Discipline

No push. Untracked junk untouched. Image tarballs live in $HOME (/tmp proved worthless again — it ate the CSRF tarball Oct 26).
